portal_hypertension.title: EUS-guided esophagogastric variceal obliteration: real-world cohort of three generation glue embolization (with video).
portal_hypertension.authors: Zhang M, Hu J, Jiang Y
portal_hypertension.zhSummary: 该文聚焦门静脉高压症，属于临床研究（样本量约为 30）。核心观点：门静脉高压患者的食管胃静脉曲张出血（EGVB）仍然危及生命。 临床提示：该真实世界队列记录了用于 GOV 型 EGVB 二级预防的逐步 EUS 引导胶栓塞演变，比较了连续方法：传统 ESVD（内镜下选择性静脉曲张断流术）
portal_hypertension.abstract: Esophagogastric variceal bleeding (EGVB) remains life-threatening in portal hypertension. This real-world cohort documents stepwise EUS-guided glue embolization evolution for secondary prophylaxis of GOV-type EGVB, comparing sequential approaches: conventional ESVD (Endoscopic selective variceal devascularization), EUS-PCSS-D/P (EUS-guided variceal puncture with cyanoacrylate selective seal targeting the distal segment of the source vessel or perforating branch vessels), and EUS-PCSS-T (targeting the source vascular trunk). We aimed to evaluate the impact of these technical iterations on clinical outcomes. Retrospective analysis of 89 patients undergoing secondary prophylaxis: ESVD (n = 30),...

portal_hypertension.title: Cirrhosis of the liver adversely affects the clinical outcomes in patients with acute pancreatitis: A propensity-matched nationwide analysis (2016-2020).
portal_hypertension.journal: Pancreatology : official journal of the International Association of Pancreatology (IAP) ... [et al.]
portal_hypertension.authors: Shah MP, Ojemolon P, Dahiya DS
portal_hypertension.zhSummary: 该文聚焦门静脉高压症，属于临床研究。核心观点：肝硬化患者由于酒精中毒和胆结石等病因的患病率较高，可能会发生急性胰腺炎（AP）。 临床提示：然而，有关 AP 和潜在肝硬化患者临床结果的数据有限。
portal_hypertension.abstract: Acute pancreatitis (AP) may develop in patients with cirrhosis of the liver due to higher prevalence of etiological factors such as alcoholism and gallstones in them. However, the data are limited regarding the clinical outcomes in patients with AP and underlying cirrhosis. National Inpatient Sample (2016-2020) was reviewed to identify adult inpatients with AP. They were divided into three groups based on presence of cirrhosis. STATA was used to compare clinical outcomes and resource utilization using multivariate and propensity score-matched analyses. 1.38 million patients were admitted with AP, with 2.2 % and 2.1 % having compensated and decompensated cirrhosis respectively.
